Transliteration: {{c1::askun fii baytii}}

{{c2::I live in my house}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — askun fii baytii

Why: hamza on alif + siin + kaaf + nuun | faa + yaa | baa + yaa + taa + yaa. Say it in beats: as · kun fii bay · tii.

How it works: askun (I live) + fii (in) + baytii (my house).

Ex: 'Both works' - with or without ana.

Class: 9/17

Text:
‎{{c1::أَنا أَسْكُن في بَيْتي}}

Transliteration: {{c1::ana askun fii baytii}}

{{c2::I live in my house}} — with ana (I)
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — ana askun fii baytii

Why: hamza on alif + nuun + alif | hamza on alif + siin + kaaf + nuun | faa + yaa | baa + yaa + taa + yaa.

How it works: ana (I) + askun (I live) + fii (in) + baytii (my house).

Class: 9/17

Cue: MSA — haadhaa waajibii

Why: haa + dhaal + alif | waaw + alif + jiim + baa + yaa. Say it in beats: haa · dhaa waa · ji · bii.

How it works: haadhaa (this) + waajib (homework) + -ii (my).

Ex: 'We don't have is in Arabic' - this + noun is already a sentence.

Class: 9/17

Cue: MSA — none; ana tamaam is shaami, her own dialect (the course tests Formal)

Why: hamza on alif + nuun + alif | taa + miim + alif + miim.

Ex: Formal: ana jayyid (man) / ana jayyida (woman).

Class: 9/17

Text:
‎{{c1::أَنا ماشي}}

Transliteration: {{c1::ana maashi}}

{{c2::I'm OK, getting along}} — Levantine
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — none; ana maashi is shaami, her own dialect (the course tests Formal)

Why: hamza on alif + nuun + alif | miim + alif + shiin + yaa.

Ex: maashi literally means 'walking' - things are moving along.

Ex: Dialect only; formal: ana jayyid / ana jayyida.

Class: 9/17

Cue: MSA — lastu

Why: laam + siin + taa. Say it in beats: las · tu.

Ex: Say lastu, not 'las-' - the final u is heard.

Ex: Follow it with an adjective; you can drop ana, since lastu already means 'I am not'.

Ex: Family: laysa (he/it is not) -> lastu (I am not).

Class: 9/17

Text:
‎{{c1::أَنا جَيِّد}}

Transliteration: {{c1::ana jayyid}}

{{c2::I'm fine, I'm good}} — said by a man
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — ana jayyid

Why: hamza on alif + nuun + alif | jiim + yaa + daal.

Ex: A woman must say ana jayyida.

Class: 9/17

Text:
‎{{c1::أَنا جَيِّدة}}

Transliteration: {{c1::ana jayyida}}

{{c2::I'm fine, I'm good}} — said by a woman
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — ana jayyida

Why: hamza on alif + nuun + alif | jiim + yaa + daal + taa marbuuTa.

How it works: jayyid (good) + -a (feminine ending).

Ex: 'Ladies, you have to say ana jayyida.'

Class: 9/17

Cue: MSA — al-khayr

Why: alif + laam + khaa + yaa + raa. Say it in beats: al · khayr.

How it works: al- (the) + khayr (good).

Ex: The same al-khayr as in SabaaH al-khayr, 'morning of the good'.

Class: 9/17, 9/29

Cue: MSA — haadhaa kitaab

Why: haa + dhaal + alif | kaaf + taa + alif + baa. Say it in beats: haa · dhaa ki · taab.

How it works: haadhaa (this) + kitaab (book) - no word for 'is'.

Ex: 'We don't have is in Arabic.'

Class: 9/17

Cue: MSA — tuuyuutaa

Why: taa + waaw + yaa + waaw + taa + alif. Say it in beats: tuu · yuu · taa.

Ex: Read it letter by letter, not from the logo. All long vowels, so no marks needed.

Class: 9/17

Cue: MSA — ithnaan

Why: alif + thaa + nuun + alif + nuun. Say it in beats: ith · naan.

Ex: Same number as ithnayn; -aan and -ayn are both the dual ending.

Class: 9/22

Text:
‎{{c1::مِن صِفْر إلى عَشَرة}}

Transliteration: {{c1::min Sifr ilaa cashara}}

{{c2::from zero to ten}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — min Sifr ilaa cashara

Why: miim + nuun | Saad + faa + raa | hamza under alif + laam + alif maqSuura | cayn + shiin + raa + taa marbuuTa.

How it works: min (from) + Sifr (zero) + ilaa (to) + cashara (ten).

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — ilaa

Why: hamza under alif + laam + alif maqSuura.

Ex: As in min Sifr ilaa cashara (from zero to ten).

Class: 9/22

Text:
‎{{c1::ـان / ـَيْن}}

Transliteration: {{c1::-aan / -ayn}}

{{c2::the dual ending: two of something}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — -aan / -ayn

Why: alif + nuun | yaa + nuun.

Ex: Arabic, like Hebrew, has singular, dual and plural.

Ex: As in ithnaan / ithnayn (two).

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — none; sitt is shaami, her own dialect (the course tests Formal)

Why: siin + taa.

Ex: Hook: English 'sit' -> sitt (lady); add -a and you get sitta (six).

Ex: 'Sitt for like an older lady'; for a woman in general Levantine says mara.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — none; mara is shaami, her own dialect (the course tests Formal)

Why: miim + raa + taa marbuuTa. Say it in beats: ma · ra.

Ex: Formal: imra'a.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — waHiid

Why: waaw + Haa + yaa + daal. Say it in beats: wa · Hiid.

Ex: Not waaHid (one): long ii = lonely, long aa = one.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — haadhihi sitt

Why: haa + dhaal + haa | siin + taa. Say it in beats: haa · dhi · hi sitt.

How it works: haadhihi (this, fem.) + sitt (lady).

Ex: haadhihi, because sitt is feminine.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — saara

Why: siin + alif + raa + taa marbuuTa. Say it in beats: saa · ra.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — cindahaa

Why: cayn + nuun + daal + haa + alif. Say it in beats: cin · da · haa.

How it works: cinda (with) + -haa (her): literally 'with her'.

Class: 9/22, 9/29

Cue: MSA — raqm

Why: raa + qaaf + miim.

Ex: She says it raqam, with a helping vowel.

Ex: She numbers exercise items raqm waaHid, raqm ithnayn, and so on.

Ex: She wants 'haadhaa raqm sabca', not the bare digit.

Class: 9/22, 9/24, 9/29

Cue: MSA — cadad

Why: cayn + daal + daal. Say it in beats: ca · dad.

Ex: raqm is a numeral (item 7); cadad is how many.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — raqm waaHid

Why: raa + qaaf + miim | waaw + alif + Haa + daal. Say it in beats: raqm waa · Hid.

How it works: raqm (number) + waaHid (one).

Class: 9/22, 9/29

Cue: MSA — laa ba's

Why: laam + alif | baa + hamza on alif + siin.

How it works: laa (no) + ba's (harm): 'no harm'.

Ex: Her use: 'How are you?' - laa ba's, 'not too strong today' but okay.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — shay'

Why: shiin + yaa + hamza.

Ex: Keep the final glottal stop in fuSHa; Levantine drops it: shii.

Ex: After a sukuun, the final hamza sits on the line.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — none; shii is shaami, her own dialect (the course tests Formal)

Why: shiin + yaa.

Ex: Formal: shay', with the final glottal stop.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — baghdaad

Why: baa + ghayn + daal + alif + daal. Say it in beats: bagh · daad.

Ex: Al-Khwarizmi worked at Baghdad's House of Wisdom in the Golden Age of Islam.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — al-khwaarizmii

Why: alif + laam + khaa + waaw + alif + raa + zaay + miim + yaa.

Ex: His Latinized name, Algoritmi, gave English 'algorithm'.

Ex: His book on Hindu numerals brought them to Europe.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — al-jabr

Why: alif + laam + jiim + baa + raa. Say it in beats: al · jabr.

How it works: al- (the) + jabr (completion).

Ex: English 'algebra' comes from al-jabr.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — hindii

Why: haa + nuun + daal + yaa. Say it in beats: hin · dii.

How it works: hind (India) + -ii ('from').

Ex: Arabs call their digits Hindi numerals - they came from India.

Class: 9/22

Cue: MSA — kaatshab

Why: kaaf + alif + taa + shiin + baa. Say it in beats: kaat · shab.

Ex: Her fun fact: ketchup is the most common chip flavor in the Arab world.

Class: 9/22

Text:
‎{{c1::اِتْفَضَّل / اِتْفَضَّلي}}

Transliteration: {{c1::itfaDDal / itfaDDalii}}

{{c2::go ahead / come in}} — Levantine; to a man / to a woman
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — none; itfaDDal / itfaDDalii is shaami, her own dialect (the course tests Formal)

Why: alif + taa + faa + Daad + laam | alif + taa + faa + Daad + laam + yaa.

Ex: Her everyday version of tafaDDal, starting with a glottal catch: it-.

Ex: On quizzes use the formal tafaDDal / tafaDDalii.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — SaaHib

Why: Saad + alif + Haa + baa. Say it in beats: Saa · Hib.

Ex: Take -ii off SaaHibii (my friend) and you have the bare word.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — SaaHiba

Why: Saad + alif + Haa + baa + taa marbuuTa. Say it in beats: Saa · Hi · ba.

How it works: SaaHib (friend) + -a (feminine ending).

Ex: Hidden t: alone it's SaaHiba, but the t comes back before a suffix - SaaHibatii.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — haadhihi SaaHibatii

Why: haa + dhaal + haa | Saad + alif + Haa + baa + taa + yaa. Say it in beats: haa · dhi · hi Saa · Hi · ba · tii.

How it works: haadhihi (this, fem.) + SaaHibatii (my friend, f.).

Ex: Feminine 'this' goes with a feminine noun.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — haadhaa SaaHibii

Why: haa + dhaal + alif | Saad + alif + Haa + baa + yaa. Say it in beats: haa · dhaa Saa · Hi · bii.

How it works: haadhaa (this) + SaaHibii (my friend).

Ex: 'Man to man, you could say [it]. No problem.'

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — brofesoor / brofesoora

Why: baa + raa + waaw + faa + yaa + siin + waaw + raa | baa + raa + waaw + faa + yaa + siin + waaw + raa + taa marbuuTa.

Ex: Arabic has no p, so it's said with b.

Ex: ustaadh / ustaadha is the real Arabic word.

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::أَنا مِن جامِعة Liberty}}

Transliteration: {{c1::ana min jaamicat Liberty}}

{{c2::I am from Liberty University}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — ana min jaamicat Liberty

Why: hamza on alif + nuun + alif | miim + nuun | jiim + alif + miim + cayn + taa marbuuTa.

How it works: ana (I) + min (from) + jaamicat (university of) + Liberty.

Ex: The t of jaamica is said because a name follows.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — akhuuka

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + waaw + kaaf. Say it in beats: a · khuu · ka.

How it works: akh (brother) + -uu- + -ka (your): brother takes a long uu before the ending.

Ex: Irregular: akhuuka, not akhuka - 'there is the u sound.'

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — ukhtii

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + taa + yaa. Say it in beats: ukh · tii.

How it works: ukht (sister) + -ii (my).

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::أُخْتُكَ / أُخْتُكِ}}

Transliteration: {{c1::ukhtuka / ukhtuki}}

{{c2::your sister}} — to a man / to a woman
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — ukhtuka / ukhtuki

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + taa + kaaf | hamza on alif + khaa + taa + kaaf.

How it works: ukht (sister) + -u + -ka / -ki (your).

Ex: Levantine drops the vowel: ukhtak / ukhtik.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — baHr

Why: baa + Haa + raa.

Ex: ibHaar (sailing) comes from the same root.

Ex: Plural: biHaar.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — baabuhu

Why: baa + alif + baa + haa. Say it in beats: baa · bu · hu.

How it works: baab (door) + -uhu (his).

Class: 9/24, 9/29

Cue: MSA — baabuhaa

Why: baa + alif + baa + haa + alif. Say it in beats: baa · bu · haa.

How it works: baab (door) + -uhaa (her).

Class: 9/24, 9/29

Cue: MSA — kitaabuhu

Why: kaaf + taa + alif + baa + haa. Say it in beats: ki · taa · bu · hu.

How it works: kitaab (book) + -uhu (his): the Damma before -hu is part of the ending.

Class: 9/24, 9/29

Cue: MSA — kitaabuhaa

Why: kaaf + taa + alif + baa + haa + alif. Say it in beats: ki · taa · bu · haa.

How it works: kitaab (book) + -uhaa (her).

Class: 9/24, 9/29

Cue: MSA — akhbaaruhu

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + baa + alif + raa + haa. Say it in beats: akh · baa · ru · hu.

How it works: akhbaar (news) + -uhu (his).

Ex: Don't mix up akhbaar (news) with akbar (greatest).

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — akhbaaruhaa

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + baa + alif + raa + haa + alif. Say it in beats: akh · baa · ru · haa.

How it works: akhbaar (news) + -uhaa (her).

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — akhuuhu

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + waaw + haa. Say it in beats: a · khuu · hu.

How it works: akh (brother) + -uu- + -hu (his): like akhuuka, brother takes a long uu.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — ukhtuhu

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + taa + haa. Say it in beats: ukh · tu · hu.

How it works: ukht (sister) + -uhu (his): 'we added the Damma on the taa' and then we added hu.'

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — Taalibuhaa

Why: Taa + alif + laam + baa + haa + alif. Say it in beats: Taa · li · bu · haa.

How it works: Taalib (student) + -uhaa (her).

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — Taalibatuhaa

Why: Taa + alif + laam + baa + taa + haa + alif. Say it in beats: Taa · li · ba · tu · haa.

How it works: Taaliba (student, f.) + -uhaa (her): the hidden t comes back.

Ex: 'Don't worry about this one' yet - the hidden t gets its own lesson soon.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — baytuhu

Why: baa + yaa + taa + haa. Say it in beats: bay · tu · hu.

How it works: bayt (house) + -uhu (his).

Ex: Levantine: bayto.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — baytuhaa

Why: baa + yaa + taa + haa + alif. Say it in beats: bay · tu · haa.

How it works: bayt (house) + -uhaa (her).

Ex: Levantine: bayta.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — waajibuka

Why: waaw + alif + jiim + baa + kaaf. Say it in beats: waa · ji · bu · ka.

How it works: waajib (homework) + -uka (your, to a man).

Ex: To a woman: waajibuki.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — waajibuhu

Why: waaw + alif + jiim + baa + haa. Say it in beats: waa · ji · bu · hu.

How it works: waajib (homework) + -uhu (his).

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — waajibuhaa

Why: waaw + alif + jiim + baa + haa + alif. Say it in beats: waa · ji · bu · haa.

How it works: waajib (homework) + -uhaa (her).

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — Saff

Why: Saad + faa.

Ex: Written with a shadda: the f is doubled.

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::أَنا طالِب في صَفّ الأُسْتاذة خوري}}

Transliteration: {{c1::ana Taalib fii Saff al-ustaadha Khouri}}

{{c2::I am a student in Professor Khouri's class}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — ana Taalib fii Saff al-ustaadha Khouri

Why: hamza on alif + nuun + alif | Taa + alif + laam + baa | faa + yaa | Saad + faa | alif + laam + hamza on alif + siin + taa + alif + dhaal + taa marbuuTa | khaa + waaw + raa + yaa.

How it works: ana (I) + Taalib (student) + fii (in) + Saff (class) + al-ustaadha (the professor) + Khouri.

Ex: Her method: 'translate every word, then put them all together.'

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::الأُسْتاذة خوري هِيَ أُسْتاذَتي}}

Transliteration: {{c1::al-ustaadha Khouri hiya ustaadhatii}}

{{c2::Professor Khouri is my professor}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — al-ustaadha Khouri hiya ustaadhatii

Why: alif + laam + hamza on alif + siin + taa + alif + dhaal + taa marbuuTa | khaa + waaw + raa + yaa | haa + yaa | hamza on alif + siin + taa + alif + dhaal + taa + yaa.

How it works: al-ustaadha Khouri + hiya (she) + ustaadhatii (my professor).

Ex: No 'is' needed: 'we don't use auxiliary verb in Arabic.'

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — ustaadhatii

Why: hamza on alif + siin + taa + alif + dhaal + taa + yaa. Say it in beats: us · taa · dha · tii.

How it works: ustaadha (professor, f.) + -ii: the hidden t comes back - ustaadhatii.

Ex: 'Since it's not ustaadhii, then it's feminine.'

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::كِتابي وَواجِبي في بَيْتي في الجامِعة}}

Transliteration: {{c1::kitaabii wa waajibii fii baytii fii al-jaamica}}

{{c2::My book and my homework are in my house, in the university}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — kitaabii wa waajibii fii baytii fii al-jaamica

Why: kaaf + taa + alif + baa + yaa | waaw + waaw + alif + jiim + baa + yaa | faa + yaa | baa + yaa + taa + yaa | faa + yaa | alif + laam + jiim + alif + miim + cayn + taa marbuuTa. Say it in beats: ki · taa · bii wa · waa · ji · bii fii bay · tii fii al · jaa · mi · ca.

How it works: kitaabii (my book) + wa (and) + waajibii (my homework) + fii (in) + baytii (my house) + fii (in) + al-jaamica (the university).

Ex: Her method: translate word by word, then put it all together.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — al-jaamica

Why: alif + laam + jiim + alif + miim + cayn + taa marbuuTa. Say it in beats: al · jaa · mi · ca.

How it works: al- (the) + jaamica (university).

Ex: Alone it's jaamica; before a name it becomes jaamicat.

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::ما اِسْم هٰذا الكِتاب؟}}

Transliteration: {{c1::maa ism haadhaa al-kitaab?}}

{{c2::What is the name of this book?}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — maa ism haadhaa al-kitaab?

Why: miim + alif | alif + siin + miim | haa + dhaal + alif | alif + laam + kaaf + taa + alif + baa. Say it in beats: maa ism haa · dhaa al · ki · taab.

How it works: maa (what) + ism (name) + haadhaa (this) + al-kitaab (the book).

Ex: Asked while holding up the Alif Baa textbook.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — al-kitaab

Why: alif + laam + kaaf + taa + alif + baa. Say it in beats: al · ki · taab.

How it works: al- (the) + kitaab (book).

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::أَخي طالِب في جامِعة Liberty. هُوَ دُكْتور.}}

Transliteration: {{c1::akhii Taalib fii jaamicat Liberty. huwa duktuur.}}

{{c2::My brother is a student at Liberty University. He is a doctor.}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — akhii Taalib fii jaamicat Liberty. huwa duktuur.

Why: hamza on alif + khaa + yaa | Taa + alif + laam + baa | faa + yaa | jiim + alif + miim + cayn + taa marbuuTa | haa + waaw | daal + kaaf + taa + waaw + raa.

How it works: akhii (my brother) + Taalib (student) + fii jaamicat Liberty; huwa (he) + duktuur (doctor).

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — duktuur

Why: daal + kaaf + taa + waaw + raa. Say it in beats: duk · tuur.

Ex: Also the title 'Dr.' - Dr. Khouri is a duktuura.

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::هُوَ مِن Virginia}}

Transliteration: {{c1::huwa min Virginia}}

{{c2::He is from Virginia}}
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — huwa min Virginia

Why: haa + waaw | miim + nuun.

How it works: huwa (he) + min (from) + Virginia.

Ex: Pattern for introducing a partner: where he or she is from.

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::واجِبُهُ لَيْسَ جَيِّد}}

Transliteration: {{c1::waajibuhu laysa jayyid}}

{{c2::His homework is not good}}

Cue: MSA — waajibuhu laysa jayyid

How it works: waajibuhu (his homework) + laysa (is not) + jayyid (good).

Ex: Strict formal grammar adds -an after laysa (jayyidan) - an ending you'll learn later.

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — amriikii

Why: hamza on alif + miim + raa + yaa + kaaf + yaa.

How it works: amriikaa (America) + -ii ('from').

Class: 9/24

Cue: MSA — amriikiyya

Why: hamza on alif + miim + raa + yaa + kaaf + yaa + taa marbuuTa. Say it in beats: am · rii · kiy · ya.

How it works: amriikii + -a (feminine): the y doubles - amriikiyya.

Class: 9/24

Text:
‎{{c1::هُوَ أَمْريكِيّ / هِيَ أَمْريكِيّة}}

Transliteration: {{c1::huwa amriikii / hiya amriikiyya}}

{{c2::He is American / she is American}}
Back Extra:
